newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BEARS' QUARTERBACK ERIK KRAMER TO MISS SIX WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-BEARS' QUARTERBACK ERIK KRAMER TO MISS SIX WEEKS.

text.p: Chicago Bears quarterback Erik Kramer revealed Monday that he will miss the next six weeks with a herniated disc in his neck.

Kramer, 31, was released from Northwestern Memorial Hospital Saturday night after tests on his upper back and neck which showed that the disc problem, just below his neck, was a result of inflammation putting pressure on the nerve.

"I didn't know that something was wrong," Kramer said. "I thought I had a back spasm. I thought I could have been hit in the back the wrong way. Normally those things take a day or two to go away, but this one never did."
"Everything to me has been presented as highly positive that I'll be back in a relatively short amount of time," Kramer added.

Kramer, the only NFL quarterback to take every snap in 1995, has struggled this season, completing 73-of-150 passes (48.7 percent) for 776 yards and three touchdowns with six interceptions in four games.
Veteran Dave Krieg started in place of Kramer Sunday and completed 16-of-30 passes for 190 yards and a touchdown in the Bears' 19-17 win over the Oakland Raiders.
Kramer set club records for attempts (522), completions (315), yards (3,838) and touchdowns (29) last season.
Kramer was signed as a free agent by the Bears in 1994.
